name: 70 Ophiuchi B

boundTo.source: El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021, MNRAS 506, 2269) list 70 Ophiuchi A and 70 Ophiuchi B in their Gaia EDR3 wide-binary catalogue (VizieR J/MNRAS/506/2269, source_id 4468557611984384512 and 4468557611977674496), 33 AU apart on the sky, with a chance-alignment probability of 3.0e-6: the pair is bound. This record adopts no orbit of the pair, so the star is placed by its own astrometry and carries no orbit.

description: A nearby orange dwarf, 67% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured by interferometry.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 702B: radius in solar radii, 0.6697 +/- 0.0089, from this work (CHARA)

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 702B: mass 0.698 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 702B: effective temperature in K, 4393 +/- 149, from this work (CHARA)

text.card: A nearby orange dwarf whose disc was measured by interferometry: 67% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Interferometry gives it 0.6697 solar radii; with its total light, that makes its surface 4,393 K.
